# SOTAs with `tags` `graphs-and-networks`

*Topics — The twenty-nine kinds of claim this anthology files against — the primary axis of both the practice registry and the reading list, and the same twenty-nine for each (ADR-026). The filing rule is the point: take a domain topic when the claim is ABOUT the domain; a claim merely discovered in one still takes its kind. The axis organizes the record, it does not bound it: content the list cannot place is evidence the list is short (ADR-059).*

**Graphs and networks** — graph-structured data and the models that run on it — node, graph and knowledge-graph embeddings, message passing and graph neural networks, their expressive power and positional encodings, graph transformers, geometric and equivariant GNNs, how they are evaluated, over-smoothing, over-squashing, curvature and rewiring, community structure and partitioning, and language models given graphs.

| [SOTA-349](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-349.md) | Before crediting a graph transformer with long-range gains, retune the message-passing baselines under the same budget, including an MLP prediction head, positional encodings and input feature normalization | Tönshoff et al. (2023), [LIT-579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-579.md) — the Long-Range Graph Benchmark's case that graph transformers are needed rested partly on untuned message-passing baselines. With a basic sweep inside the same 500k-parameter budget, GCN beats GPS on both Peptides tasks. Most of the gain is from replacing a linear prediction head with a 2-layer MLP. Normalizing input features lifts every model on the superpixel tasks, where GPS still leads. Tune both sides before attributing a gap to attention. | Active |
| [SOTA-350](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-350.md) v2 | Compare GNN architectures over many random data splits and seeds, with one shared training and hyperparameter-selection procedure for every model, never on a single fixed split | Shchur et al. (2018), [LIT-581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-581.md) — on the Planetoid split GAT beats GCN. On another random split of the same size GCN wins, and averaged over 100 splits × 20 seeds with identical training and tuning, GCN ranks first of four GNNs. A single split selects the model that overfits it, and per-model recipes measure the recipe. Errica et al. (2020), LIT-838, find the same for graph classification, where a graph-agnostic baseline beats every GNN on three of four chemical datasets. Report mean and spread over many splits and seeds, with the same tuning budget for every model. | Active |
| [SOTA-351](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-351.md) v2 | In a message-passing GNN for graph-level tasks, aggregate neighbours by sum with an MLP update, not by mean or max, when graph structure rather than node features carries the signal | Xu et al. (2019), [LIT-580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-580.md) — mean and max aggregation cannot count neighbors, so graphs that differ only in counts look the same to them. On featureless Reddit graphs, mean-aggregation GNNs are at chance (50.0, 20.0) and sum–MLP scores 92.4 and 57.5, which are validation accuracies across folds; held out, GIN scores 87.0 and 53.8. With informative node features the choice matters much less, and results are mostly within noise. Use h = MLP((1 + ε)h + Σ neighbors) with ε = 0 and a sum readout. | Active |
| [SOTA-450](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-450.md) | Evaluate graph models on a split that follows the application, by time, scaffold, species or target, and do not report a random split's score as the expected performance | Hu et al. (2020), [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md) — for the same model at the same split ratio, a random split scores higher than the application's split on every dataset the authors checked: by 1.8 points on ogbn-arxiv, 9.7 on ogbn-products, 5.7 ROC-AUC on ogbg-molhiv, 22.5 on ogbg-ppa and 27.0 Hits@20 on ogbl-ddi. On the random splits the train–test gap nearly vanishes. If the model will meet later data, new scaffolds, new species or new targets, split that way and report that number. | Active |
| [SOTA-452](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-452.md) | Give a message-passing GNN random-walk positional encodings, or Laplacian eigenvectors through a sign-invariant encoder, rather than raw Laplacian eigenvectors with random sign flips | Dwivedi et al. (2022), [LIT-833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md), and Lim et al. (2023), [LIT-818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-818.md). On ZINC with the same GatedGCN and about 500k parameters, Laplacian eigenvectors with random sign flips give test MAE 0.202 and 0.198 in the two papers. Random-walk return probabilities (RWPE) at the input give 0.122, and the same 8 eigenvectors through SignNet give 0.121. For GINE and PNA, flipped eigenvectors are no better than no encoding. On OGB molecules, whose features already mark rings, every gain is under 2%. | Proposed |
| [SOTA-453](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-453.md) | Before crediting a knowledge-graph embedding score function, train the baselines with the same loss, negative sampling and embedding size | Sun et al. (2019), [LIT-819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-819.md) — RotatE's main tables beat TransE's reported FB15k-237 MRR of 0.294 with 0.338. Trained with RotatE's own self-adversarial negative sampling, loss and 1000 dimensions, TransE reaches 0.332, and the authors note it then beats every earlier model on that dataset. On FB15k, which needs symmetric relations TransE cannot represent, the gap survives (0.797 against 0.735). Give every score function the same training before attributing a gap to the score function. | Proposed |
| [SOTA-454](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-454.md) | When putting a graph into a frozen LLM prompt to ask about a node's neighbours or degree, write each node followed by its neighbours, with integer ids, not a flat edge list or named-entity relations | Fatemi et al. (2023), [LIT-807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-807.md) — "Node 2 is connected to nodes 0, 1, 3" puts a node's neighbourhood in one span. On PaLM 62B it beats an edge list on connected-nodes and degree questions under all five prompting methods: 53.8 against 19.8 zero-shot on connected nodes, 75.2 against 66.8 on degree with CoT-BAG. On PaLM 2 L zero-shot the gap is 88.0 against 55.6 and 85.0 against 49.6. Integer ids beat names on numeric answers by far more. It is task-specific: the edge list wins on edge count, and on the smallest PaLM 2 the advantage disappears. | Proposed |
| [SOTA-455](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-455.md) | On a graph-level task that depends on interactions between distant nodes, make the last message-passing layer fully adjacent before reaching for a wider model | Alon and Yahav (2020), [LIT-839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-839.md) — in the last layer only, connect every pair of nodes, keeping the layer type, the weights and the hyperparameters. On QM9, with eight-layer models tuned by Brockschmidt, this cut mean error by 42% across six GNNs, where doubling the width cut it by 5.5%. On NCI1 and VarMisuse the gains are mostly within one standard deviation. Making every layer fully adjacent was far worse. Proposed: one group, no retuning, and a quadratic cost in the last layer. | Proposed |
| [SOTA-456](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-456.md) | In a graph transformer, keep a local message-passing layer beside global attention in every block, rather than relying on attention and positional encodings alone | Rampášek et al. (2022), [LIT-842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-842.md) — in GPS ablations on six datasets, removing the message-passing layer from each block costs more than removing global attention: ZINC MAE 0.070 to 0.217 without it, unchanged without attention. Exphormer ([LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md)) finds the same with sparse attention on five more. Shown at benchmark scale, up to 6M parameters; whether it holds with much more data, or against attention biased by graph distance, is open. | Active |
| [SOTA-457](../../../record/practices.d/SOTA-457.md) | In a message-passing GNN for graph-level prediction, try a virtual node connected to every node, and keep it only if validation favors it | Hu et al. (2020), [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), and Gilmer et al. (2017), [LIT-829](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-829.md) — a node joined to every other node gives each message-passing step a global channel. In OGB's baselines it lifts GIN from 22.66 to 27.03 AP on ogbg-molpcba and leaves GIN comparable or better on 9 of 10 further MoleculeNet sets, but leaves GCN level on ogbg-molhiv. In the MPNN paper a master node cuts QM9 error by about a quarter without geometry. Treat it as a cheap option to validate, not a default. | Proposed |
